pluginActionRequest.description: Repairs one faulty entry in a Docker CLI plugin directory. Neither action installs anything: the core has no HTTP client and cannot execute anything but the fingerprinted Docker binary. 'remove' unlinks the entry, which is the only remedy for a symlink whose target a package manager deleted; 'enable' adds the execute bit the CLI requires. The core re-derives the entry's faulty classification itself and refuses a path outside the CLI's own plugin directories.

name.description: The plugin command name, without the 'docker-' file prefix.

pluginPath.description: Absolute path of the plugin entry being repaired. The core additionally requires the parent directory to be one the Docker CLI searches and the file name to begin with 'docker-'; this pattern only keeps the value off the shapes that would read as a flag or carry a control character.

composeProject.description: Compose project name. Becomes an argv element and a label selector; Compose itself normalizes to this shape.

ref.description: builder/node/id or a bare record id. Separators may appear inside a segment but never first, since a leading '-' would read as a flag.

buildsBuilderActionRequest.description: Runs one of buildx's own builder verbs. 'bootstrap' is `buildx inspect --bootstrap`, the repair for a builder buildx reports as unreachable; 'remove' is `buildx rm`, which discards the builder and its cache. `buildx use` is deliberately absent: it rewrites the CLI configuration every tool on the machine reads.

name.description: Builder name. Separators may appear inside it, as in Docker's own `desktop-linux`, but never first, since a leading '-' would read as a flag.

params.description: Docker has no clone verb; the contents are streamed from the source's helper into a helper on a target that must not already exist.
Discards every byte the volume holds; Docker cannot empty in place, so the volume is removed and recreated from its own declaration.
Compose finds a running project by label but cannot render a configuration it was never given, so the files are required exactly as they are for up.

containersRebindPortsRequest.description: Republishes a container's ports by replacing it. Docker fixes bindings at creation and `docker update` cannot change them, so the core creates a new container from the original's own Config and HostConfig with only the port fields replaced. The container ID changes, the writable layer is discarded, and the log history goes with it — which is why `confirmed` is mandatory. Note that `id` is bounded rather than pinned to a full 64-character ID, matching what the core accepts here; every other container verb requires the immutable form.

ports.description: Host port to container port, as in containers.create. An empty map publishes nothing.

secretsListRequest.description: Lists Swarm secret references. There is no inspect verb and no write verb: Docker never returns a secret's value after creation, and creating or removing one is out of scope for this protocol version.

archivePath.description: Absolute host path for save/load/export. A leading '-' is rejected because the value becomes an argv element next to a Docker flag; the core additionally canonicalizes the parent directory against the working-directory allowlist.
